title: Immutable Audit Marshal: region-aware WORM retention + evidence export
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build an "Audit Marshal" subsystem: an append-only, region-aware audit capture and long-term evidence layer that ingests admin actions, privileged access events, and configuration changes; enforces residency and retention policies; produces cryptographic attestations (KMS/HSM-signed manifests); and provides an automated evidence export/reporting API for legal/forensics and SOC teams. This ticket scopes the core data model, ingestion pipeline, WORM-backed storage adapters, attestation format, verification tooling, and rollout plan for Dedicated/Private customers.
motivation: Customers in regulated industries require tamper-evident admin logs that cannot be altered, with proof of retention and automated evidence exports for audits and legal holds. Existing ephemeral logs in the runtime and console do not meet WORM or residency guarantees and lack a reproducible attestation chain.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ingest pipeline accepts admin events and writes append-only records with per-event metadata (region, tenant, source, sequence) to the Audit Marshal.
2) Daily and on-demand signed manifests are generated and stored in region-specific WORM buckets (or on-prem equivalent) and are queryable by evidence APIs.
3) Each manifest includes a cryptographic hash summary plus KMS/HSM timestamp signature; manifest signature can be verified with a provided verification tool.
4) Retention rules (per-customer, per-region) are enforced by the retention engine; deletion requests are rejected when retention is active and produce audit evidence.
5) End-to-end tests and canary rollout plan executed in staging with no measurable impact on 99th percentile API latency for hosted customers.
6) Documentation and runbook for SOC & legal teams complete.
design_decisions:
- Store raw event stream in hot append-only block store (Kafka/ledger) for short-term reads; flush compacted day partitions to region-specific WORM targets (S3 Object Lock or on-prem write-once hardware).
- Use cloud KMS for signature generation for hosted; integrate HSM-backed signing for Private customers.
- Manifests will use SHA-256 Merkle-root over ordered event batches to provide tamper-evidence while keeping per-object size small.
- Export format: JSONL events + JSON manifest with signature and provenance metadata.
- Verification tool distributed as a small CLI (Go) to validate manifest->object integrity and timestamp signature.
- Trade-offs: object-lock increases storage cost and complicates live query; we provide a secondary index store for queryable slices (search index that references immutable objects).
tasks: Define Audit Marshal event schema and storage envelope
Implement ingestion adapter in runtime to emit structured admin events
Provision append-only ledger (Kafka + retention-safe topology) and daily compaction job
Implement WORM sink adapters: S3 Object Lock writer, on-prem file system writer, GCS Locked buckets adapter
Integrate KMS signing and HSM signing hooks for manifests
Build manifest generator and signer service + verification CLI
Retention enforcement engine with residency awareness and policy evaluation
Evidence API for exports, legal holds, and quick attestations
Add audit events to Console UI & export connectors to SIEM/Offboard pipelines
E2E tests, load tests, and cost model analysis
risks_and_open_questions: How to guarantee cross-region evidence equivalence when customer data must stay in a single region? (solution: manifest per-region; cross-region only metadata pointers)
Cost of storing full event payloads long-term vs storing compressed digests and indexed pointers
KMS/HSM integration for Private: what partners/APIs are required and what latency SLA for signing?
Queryability: how to allow reasonable forensic queries without breaking immutability guarantees?
Backward compatibility with legacy audit streams and tenant mappings
test_plan:
- Unit tests for schema & signer.
- Integration tests: ingest synthetic admin events -> flush -> manifest signed -> verification CLI validates hashes.
- Load test: simulate 100k admin events/day and validate compaction latency and signer throughput.
- Retention tests: simulate legal-hold + deletion attempt; expect rejection with audit evidence.
- Canary: enable for internal tenant group for 2 weeks, monitor CPU/latency and storage costs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary (internal-redwood). Phase 2: opt-in beta for 3 enterprise customers (Dedicated). Phase 3: general availability for Hosted + Dedicated + Private with migration tool for legacy logs. GA only after security review and SOC playbook sign-off.
